About the Mankind Divided Pre-order Shenanigans - I Don't Think It's As Bad As Some Are Saying, Might Even Be a Good Thing

Pixeljudge is wrong and has missed the point.

There are three complaints that are at the core of things

  1. You cannot get "the whole experience" of the game without pre-ordering. This means that you have to purchase something sight-unseen to get the full game. Which is distasteful.

  2. This method of pre-orders turns people who haven't even played the game into salesmen for the game, because they get more rewards for having more people purchase the game.

  3. More pre orders means the release date moves up. Implying that the release date is not set by actually having the game finished, just that the release date is set by people who want to milk more money out of the fanbase.

Pixeljudge's whole point is that you get all the rewards if you purchase a pre-order. Which would be true, if everyone goes out and works as salesmen for a game that hasn't come out yet.

However, this paragraph takes the cake in terms of true idiocy. I'll let you read for yourselves if you haven't the patience for the whole thing

It's also worth remembering that this system appears to have been decided upon, at least in part, by the Deus Ex community. Though it has proven difficult to find any conclusive evidence of this beyond Squeenix's claim that it is so. But it has proven equally difficult to find any evidence that this is not the case, and we can be fairly confident that a misrepresented fanbase would not stay silent on such a matter. Leaving us to believe that the complaints are being levied not by the core fans, but a more distant element who are displeased with, perhaps, a skewed understanding of the event and a negative interpretation of Squeenix's motives.

1/ That's flatly untrue. Anyone who buys the Collector's Edition and, in fact, only those who buy the Collector's Edition will get all the rewards. I even stated that in the linked piece.

2/ Agreed, and this is one of the valid criticisms I alluded to, but did not expound on.

3/ A grey area which, again, I am inclined to agree with.

To clarify, I am not saying this is in and of itself a good thing. That was poorly worded on my part. What I am saying is that, like it or not, pre-orders work. They aren't going away any time soon. At least in an instance like this, there is more to gain from a pre-order than simply the game. So it might be better worded to say that this is less bad than the alternative
1. I'm comparing non-pre-orders to pre-orders. If you don't pre-order, you get jack-didlly-squat.

If you buy the standard version post release, yes, you do get less. I'm not saying that it's a good thing. But it is better than we usually see. Where a pre-order also gives you fuck all. Ergo, it's the most consumer friendly way a pre-order has, thus far, been handled by a large publisher

The argument is based on some of the outrage being based on false details. But it ignores the fact that the scheme itself is designed to build "faithful" in an effort to increase sales of a game that doesn't even have a critical review at this stage. Fuck that mind controlling nonsense.

Dressing the whole thing up with language like "innovative", "interesting" and "consumer choice" is just fabrication and biased idiocy. Guess who won't see anything but archived links from now on, that's right it's pixeljudge you damn sellouts.

I didn't say it was consumer choice, they did. I don't recall saying it was innovative either. Nor, might I add, did I even claim it was a positive thing in and of itself. Only that it is better than pre-ordering a game solely to buy the game

Here come the apologists.

Putting aside the issues some people have with pre-ordering as a concept

I don't understand this phrase at all. The whole issue IS with preordering. Why even write a defense if your first word is to disregard the whole issue? It's like telling someone that hit his thumb with a hammer, that it doesn't hurt because we should disregard his thumb.

everyone who pre-orders has access to all tiers at a flat price.

No they don't. They have a CHANCE to get access to all tiers at a flat price, assuming enough people are stupid enough to fall for this. If not enough people preorder it, they'll get nothing of all the promised rewards. It's a total bait and switch. You're not preordering, you're buying the CHANCE that you might preorder. You're not being guaranteed anything.

There are certainly still valid complaints to be made. Limiting in game items to people who pay certain amounts at a certain time, or buy from x distributor and so on, is a problem that is annoyingly prevalent within the gaming world. But at the same time, such items are rarely genuinely game breaking, and are more like neat little perks to those who want a little extra, as opposed to a detriment to those without them. Much in the same way that DLC armour or weapons add to a game. Though that's a whole different kettle of fish.

I honestly don't give a crap if they're game breaking or not. The fact that they're there is reason enough for me to not buy it, because I want to buy whole games, not chopped up episodic DLC platforms. The Witcher devs have done extremely well with their latest games, without having to resort to this kind of bullshit. They're releasing a new DLC FOR FREE. Meanwhile, these jokers try and rope you in with vague promises and rewards which might or might not be good, in a game you haven't seen or played yet. That's a big financial risk to ask someone to take, for a reward that shouldn't even be a reward.

It's also worth remembering that this system appears to have been decided upon, at least in part, by the Deus Ex community. Though it has proven difficult to find any conclusive evidence of this beyond Squeenix's claim that it is so.

The internet never forgets. If the evidence was there, you can bet your ass Squeenix would have put it forward by now. But hey, with this kind of logic, I would like to sell the article writer a digital edition rock that keeps away Siberian internet viruses. The truth of the matter is, beyond the concerns some gamers have regarding the purpose of pre-ordering in and of itself, this is genuinely one of the most consumer friendly ways a publisher has ever approached it.

No it isn't, it's an affront to consumers to not only ask them to invest in a game they've never seen, but also invest in the CHANCE of getting preorders. It's a double bait and switch. And really, this article is the height of apologism. It stinks of shilling.

in short, this whole thing is very much a mountain made out of a molehill.

And in closing, we're seeing the classic shill 101 bullshit retort: If you can't beat your opponents arguments, ridicule their stance.

Seriously, to whomever wrote this article, I would just like to extend my middle finger and tell you to go shill somewhere else.
